abstract:
Sequence-sum policy-gradient estimators in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) carry nonzero signed token mass ($\sum_{i=1}^G L_i w_i 
eq 0$) whenever positive and negative trajectories have different mean lengths, inducing length drift. Enforcing per-group zero signed token mass ($\sum_{i=1}^G L_i w_i = 0$ on every realization) eliminates this pressure, while Pass@K Policy Optimization (PKPO) replaces $\operatorname{pass@}1$ with $\operatorname{pass@}k(q;	heta) = 1 - (1-p(q;	heta))^k$ or $\operatorname{all@}m(q;	heta) = p(q;	heta)^m$. We ask whether a finite-sample on-policy group estimator can simultaneously satisfy exact per-realization zero signed token mass and remain an unbiased estimator, up to a parameter-independent constant $\alpha_0

First, for any fixed sample budget $N \ge 2$ and sample-only weight map $w_i(r_{1:N}, L_{1:N})$ with $\sum_{i=1}^N L_i w_i = 0$, the expected gradient on two-length binary policies factors universally as $\mathbb{E}_p[L]\,Q(p;\ell_+,\ell_-)\,

Second, Bernstein basis independence uniquely determines the count-stratum weights achieving $ rac{\mathbb{E}_p[L]}{C}

Third, while this estimator prevents within-question directional rotation when lengths and scores co-vary, its $\mathbb{E}_	heta[L \mid q]/C$ factor can strictly invert the multi-question $\operatorname{pass@}k$ ascent direction. Fourth, statistically independent per-question length normalizers preserve conditional within-question collinearity. A zero-dependency Python rational-arithmetic checker verifies all finite-policy claims.

title: When per-group token-mass balance preserves or inverts pass@k policy gradients
